title: Chicken Chilaquiles Verdes with Cotija & Red Onion
dek: Roasted tomatillo salsa, tender shredded chicken and sturdy tortilla chips come together in a bright, savory skillet finished with cool crema, Cotija, red onion and cilantro.
image_alt: Chicken chilaquiles verdes with salsa-coated tortilla chips, crumbled white cheese, thin red onion and fresh cilantro in a black bowl
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb tomatillos, husked, rinsed and halved
1 medium poblano pepper, halved lengthwise and seeded
1 small jalapeño, halved lengthwise and seeded for mild heat
1/2 medium white onion, cut into 4 wedges
1 packed cup cilantro leaves and tender stems, divided
3 cups shredded cooked chicken, about 14 oz
12 oz thick restaurant-style corn tortilla chips
1/3 cup Mexican crema or sour cream thinned with 1 tbsp water
1/3 cup very thinly sliced red onion
Hot sauce or sliced fresh jalapeño, for serving

instructions.name: Heat the broiler and prepare the vegetables
instructions.text: Position a rack 6 inches below the broiler and heat it to high. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil. Arrange the tomatillos cut-side down with the poblano, jalapeño, onion wedges and unpeeled garlic. Rub with 1 tablespoon oil. Keep the vegetables in a single layer so they blister instead of steaming.

instructions.name: Broil the salsa vegetables
instructions.text: Broil for 8 to 10 minutes, rotating the pan once, until the tomatillos have collapsed and developed dark spots and the peppers and onion are blistered at their edges. Remove the garlic after 6 minutes if it softens early. Cool for 3 minutes, then peel the garlic.

instructions.name: Blend the salsa verde
instructions.text: Transfer the roasted vegetables and every pan juice to a blender. Add 3/4 cup broth, 3/4 cup cilantro and 1 teaspoon salt. Vent the lid for hot liquid, cover the opening with a folded towel and blend from low to high until mostly smooth, about 30 seconds. Keep hands clear of the vent.

instructions.name: Simmer the sauce and chicken
instructions.text: Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in a wide 12-inch skillet over medium. Carefully pour in the salsa; it will sputter. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring often, until slightly thickened. Stir in the chicken and remaining 1/4 cup broth. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F. Taste and add the remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt only if needed.

instructions.name: Coat the chips without making them soggy
instructions.text: Reserve 1 cup chips for the crisp topping. Add the remaining chips to the simmering salsa and fold gently with a wide spatula for 45 to 60 seconds, just until every chip is coated and the edges begin to soften. Remove the skillet from the heat immediately; the chips continue absorbing sauce as they stand.

instructions.name: Finish and serve
instructions.text: Divide the chilaquiles among four shallow bowls. Top with the reserved crisp chips, Cotija, crema, red onion, avocado and the remaining cilantro. Serve at once with lime wedges. Keep the base mild and offer hot sauce or fresh jalapeño at the table.

why_it_works: Broiling tomatillos, poblano, onion and garlic concentrates their flavor while dark blistered spots add depth without the time required for a long stovetop salsa.
Warming fully cooked chicken in the salsa brings it safely to 165°F and seasons every shred before the chips enter the skillet.
A brief fold off the heat plus a final handful of dry chips creates the defining chilaquiles contrast: saucy centers with crisp edges and fresh, cool toppings.
swaps: For a meatless version, replace the chicken with 2 drained 15-ounce cans of pinto or black beans and use low-sodium vegetable broth; heat the beans until steaming throughout before adding the chips.
Use queso fresco or mild feta in place of Cotija. Queso fresco is softer and less salty, so taste the salsa before withholding the final salt.
For a shortcut, replace the homemade salsa with 3 cups refrigerated salsa verde. Simmer it for 5 minutes, thinning with broth only as needed, then continue with the chicken.
storage: Chilaquiles are best served immediately. For meal prep, refrigerate the salsa and chicken together in a shallow airtight container for up to 4 days and keep the chips and toppings separate. Reheat the salsa-chicken mixture in a skillet over medium until it reaches 165°F, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons broth if thick, then fold in fresh chips. Refrigerate assembled leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 1 day; reheating is safe to 165°F, but the chips will be soft.
notes: Choose thick, sturdy corn tortilla chips; thin snack chips break down before they can be evenly coated.
Rotisserie chicken should be refrigerated within 2 hours of purchase or serving and reheated to 165°F in this recipe. Discard perishable food left out more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F.
Tomatillos naturally vary in tartness. Blend the salsa before adding extra lime; the fresh lime wedges at the table are easier to adjust serving by serving.
The written jalapeño amount is deliberately mild. Leave in some seeds for more heat, or keep the skillet mild and use hot sauce at the table.

faqs.q: How do I keep chilaquiles from turning completely soggy?
faqs.a: Use thick chips, simmer the salsa until lightly thickened before the chips go in and fold for no more than one minute. Plate immediately and add the reserved dry chips on top so every serving retains crunch.

faqs.q: Can I make the salsa verde ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Cool the blended salsa quickly and refrigerate it airtight for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat it to a full simmer, then add the cooked chicken and continue with fresh chips.

faqs.q: Are chilaquiles the same as nachos?
faqs.a: No. Nachos are typically baked or broiled with toppings while keeping the chips crisp. Chilaquiles briefly cook the chips in warm salsa, creating tender, sauce-soaked centers while some edges remain firm.
